abstract: Inferring spatial gene expression from histology images offers a promising strategy for extending spatial molecular profiling to large-scale clinical tissue archives. However, existing approaches face two major challenges: limited generalizability of single-cell expression inference across datasets and platforms, and the lack of reliable estimates of prediction uncertainty, which compromise downstream biological and clinical analyses. Here, we present REGAIN, a framework for spatial gene expression inference at both single-cell and spot resolutions with prediction confidence. Across tissue sections, independent datasets and platforms, REGAIN improved spatial gene expression prediction and downstream analysis. Confidence-guided selection further enriched for cells with more accurately recovered expression profiles and improved cell-type annotation, while confidence-weighted clustering enhanced spatial-domain identification. Beyond assessing prediction quality, confidence mapping reveals greater heterogeneity in gene expression predictability across spatial domains than across broad cell types, with differences persisting within the same cell type and associated with tumor progression-related cell states and local microenvironmental context. Importantly, in 766 patients from the TCGA-BRCA cohort, confidence weighting enhanced the prognostic value of histology-inferred spatial molecular features, yielding stronger prognostic associations and identifying additional prognostic information beyond age and PAM50 molecular subtype. These confidence-weighted features also showed improved prognostic discrimination compared with clinical variables alone or combined with unweighted spatial molecular features. Together, REGAIN marks a shift in histology-based spatial gene expression inference from a focus on predictive accuracy toward a reliability-aware paradigm, demonstrating that prediction confidence provides biological insights into morphology-expression coupling and enhances the clinical informativeness of inferred spatial molecular features.
